session_meta.research_objective:
Focus group guide exploring how men in the UK make everyday food
choices, how social context, work, hobbies, health, taste and other
people shape what they eat, how gender and masculinity may influence
food choices, and what would need to change for plant-based foods to
become more acceptable or appealing.
session_meta.topic_domain: Masculinity, food choice, animal product consumption, and plant-based eating
session_meta.participant_collective_identity: Men in the UK reflecting on food choices, male friendship, gender norms, and plant-based eating
session_meta.moderator_knowledge_brief:
Explore (1) everyday food decision-making, (2) the social contexts in
which men spend time with male friends, (3) the influence of other
people, work, hobbies, health, nutrition and taste on food choices,
(4) whether participants perceive gender as shaping what they eat,
(5) social acceptability and gendered meanings attached to vegetarian,
vegan, plant-based, feminine or masculine foods, and (6) what personal,
social and practical changes would make plant-based eating more viable
or appealing. The discussion should remain exploratory, non-judgmental,
and non-leading.

discussion_guide.scripted_question:
Hi everyone, thanks so much for joining the focus group today. We’re
going to take about 45 minutes to talk about your food choices and
opinions, and this will be recorded for research purposes. Try not to
overthink the questions, and simply speak freely. There are no right
or wrong answers. Please be respectful of your fellow focus group
members, and keep your responses relatively brief to allow time for
everyone to speak. But remember that this is a conversation, not an
interview, so you can jump in when you have something to say and you
don’t have to take turns answering each question, but you can if you
want to. Okay great, let’s start by going around and saying your name
and where in the UK you’re coming from today.

discussion_guide.section_label: Opening discussion: male friendship and place
discussion_guide.section_purpose: Section 1: Opening discussion: male friendship and place
discussion_guide.scripted_question:
What’s your favourite place in your city to spend time with your male
friends? Why? Feel free to be specific.
How do you decide what to eat?
suggested_probes: Do other people influence what you eat? If so, tell us more about how.
Do your work or hobbies influence what foods you eat? Tell us more about how.
How important is health and nutrition?

discussion_guide.scripted_question:
Do you think your gender influences what you eat? Tell us more about
why or why not.
suggested_probes: Is it socially acceptable for men to eat vegetarian or vegan foods?

discussion_guide.scripted_question:
Imagine you decided to go plant-based — what would need to change in
your life for you to do that?
suggested_probes: How would your family and friends react to this?
How might it change the way you shop or cook?

discussion_guide.section_purpose: Section 5: Making plant-based foods more appealing
discussion_guide.scripted_question:
What might make plant-based foods more appealing to you or other men
you know?

Okay everyone, that’s our time. Thanks so much for participating
today. Before we finish, is there anything else you would like to add
about food choices, gender, masculinity, or plant-based eating?

mm_fg3_andrew.name: Andrew
mm_fg3_andrew.profile_summary: Andrew, 45, Male. Suburban, South East, UK.

background.working_life: A forty-five-year-old employee working full-time as a manager in logistics, warehousing and transport, within the wholesale and retail trade and motor vehicle repair sector. The role carries supervisory responsibility for a team, placing it in the lower managerial and administrative bracket, and typically involves between thirty-one and forty-eight hours each week. A degree-level qualification underpins the career. The workplace sits between ten and twenty kilometres from home, reached by car or van, with no element of the job carried out remotely.
background.home_and_household: Home is a terraced house in a suburban part of the South East, owned with a mortgage. The household consists of one person aged under sixty-five, living alone, never married and never in a registered civil partnership. There are at least two more bedrooms than the occupancy standard requires, so spare rooms are available for storage, a study or occasional guests. Maintaining the property, keeping up with mortgage payments and managing routine repairs and bills fall entirely to the single occupant.
background.week_and_hobbies: Weekdays follow a settled rhythm shaped by shift patterns and a twenty-minute or so commute by car, with early starts common in transport management. Evenings at home tend to be quiet, given over to television, music, reading or catching up on household admin. Spare rooms allow space for a desk, tools or hobby equipment. Weekends leave room for car maintenance, garden and DIY tasks, driving out to the coast or countryside, and keeping in touch with friends and wider family.

mm_fg3_daniel.name: Daniel
mm_fg3_daniel.profile_summary: Daniel, 48, Male. Suburban, East of England, UK.

background.working_life: A forty-eight-year-old employee in the construction sector, working in the building finishing trades and classed within routine occupations. Employment is full-time, typically between thirty-one and forty-eight hours a week, with supervisory responsibility for others on site. There is no fixed place of work, so tasks are carried out at whatever property or development is currently contracted, reached by driving a car or van. Skills were gained through an apprenticeship, which remains the highest formal qualification held, and practical experience accumulated over many years on varied jobs.
background.home_and_household: Home is a detached house in a suburban part of the East of England, owned with a mortgage still being repaid. The household consists of two adults, both aged sixty-five or under: a married couple in an opposite-sex partnership, with no dependent children living with them. Recorded as the husband or wife of the household reference person. The property has two or more bedrooms beyond the notional requirement, so there is considerable spare room, including space that can be given over to storage or occasional visitors.
background.week_and_hobbies: Weekdays follow the rhythm of site work, with early starts, driving between locations across the region, and an evening return to the suburban house. Time away from work tends to be spent on maintenance and improvement of the property and garden, alongside vehicle upkeep and occasional projects using trade tools already to hand. Weekends allow for longer drives, visits to relatives and friends, following sport and motoring interests, and quieter evenings at home with a spouse who is also of working age.

mm_fg3_john.name: John
mm_fg3_john.profile_summary: John, 45, Male. Suburban, South West, UK.

background.working_life: A self-employed road transport driver in his mid-forties, working full-time on his own account without staff or supervisory duties. His work sits within the transport and storage sector, and he holds no formal qualifications, having built his experience through years behind the wheel. Weeks routinely run to forty-nine hours or more, with schedules shaped by delivery windows and depot timings rather than fixed office hours. He travels to a workplace between ten and twenty kilometres away, driving a van or car there himself.
background.home_and_household: He rents a detached house from a private landlord in a suburban part of the South West. The property is larger than the household strictly requires, with two or more bedrooms spare under standard occupancy measures. Two adults share the home, both aged sixty-five or under, and there are no children living there. He is divorced and not currently living as part of a couple. The arrangement is a private tenancy rather than ownership, giving a settled base without the commitments of a mortgage.
background.week_and_hobbies: Long working hours leave limited free time, and much of the week is structured around early starts and late finishes. Quieter evenings tend to be spent at home, with radio, television and motorsport coverage among the usual distractions. Weekends allow for vehicle maintenance, tinkering in the driveway, and occasional drives out towards the coast or open countryside within reach of the South West suburbs. Contact with the other adult in the household is informal, and social plans are generally arranged around the shifting rota.

mm_fg3_nick.name: Nick
mm_fg3_nick.profile_summary: Nick, 40, Male. Suburban, North West, UK.

background.working_life: A forty-year-old employee working full-time in an electrical and electronic trade within the information and communication sector, typically between thirty-one and forty-eight hours each week. There is no fixed place of work, so days are spent moving between client premises and installation points rather than a single office or depot. He drives a car or van to reach each assignment, carrying tools and test equipment. He holds no supervisory or management responsibility, instead working to job schedules, and is qualified to degree level or professional equivalent.
background.home_and_household: Home is a semi-detached house in a suburban part of the North West, owned with a mortgage. Three people live there: himself, his wife, and their one dependent child, who is under five. The property has one bedroom more than the household strictly requires, giving a little spare space for storage or a small study area. Being an owner with a loan shapes monthly budgeting, and the household runs as two adults sharing responsibility for a young child alongside full-time paid work.
background.week_and_hobbies: Weekdays follow a driving-based pattern, with early starts and travel time between jobs, so evenings at home tend to be quiet and centred on a very young child's routine. Weekends bring trips to local parks and soft play, visits to relatives, and steady work on the house and garden. Practical interests reflect his trade: tinkering with wiring, audio equipment, computing and home automation projects. He also follows sport on television, reads technical material online, and occasionally studies for further professional certification.

mm_fg3_paul.name: Paul
mm_fg3_paul.profile_summary: Paul, 47, Male. Suburban, South East, UK.

background.working_life: A forty-seven-year-old employee working full-time, typically between thirty-one and forty-eight hours a week, in a lower professional and higher technical role. The work sits within human resources, training and vocational guidance, supporting people through recruitment processes, learning programmes and career development. The employing organisation operates in administrative and support service activities. There are no supervisory or management responsibilities attached to the post, and the role is carried out mainly at or from home rather than at a separate workplace. Formal qualifications amount to a small number of GCSE-level or vocational credits.
background.home_and_household: Home is a terraced house in a suburban part of the South East of England, owned with a mortgage still being repaid. The household contains two people: a married couple of opposite sexes, both aged sixty-five or under, with no children living with them and no dependants in the family. The property has at least two more bedrooms than the household requires, so one room can readily serve as a study or workspace. Household responsibilities and running costs are shared between the two adults.
background.week_and_hobbies: Weekdays follow a steady rhythm shaped by working from home, with no commute and a spare room set aside as an office. Breaks are often spent outdoors on local suburban streets and green spaces, and the absence of travelling time leaves room for reading, listening to music and keeping up with practical courses online. Weekends allow for maintenance jobs around the terraced house and garden, occasional day trips within the South East, and quiet time spent with a spouse.
